en: The Basket of Conduct (Cariyāpiṭaka),
Elephant-Naga Chapter,
Perfection of Virtue (Sīlapāramī) 2
The Bhūridatta Jātaka: “Furthermore,
when I was the powerful Bhūridatta;”
By the great king Virūpakkha,
I went to the world of the gods.
There, having seen the devas, I—
Being entirely absorbed in happiness,
I undertook rules and observances for the sake of going to heaven.
Having performed the bodily duties and eaten only what is necessary for sustenance,
one should resolve upon the four factors.
Halfway up the anthill.
“By skin, by hide, by flesh,
Or by sinews, bones, or marrow;”
"Let him who has need of it take what has been given; let the ungrateful one depart disgraced."
Āḷampāyana seized me;
having placed me in a basket, he played with me here and there.
Even when they throw me into a basket or crush me with their hands,
I do not become angry at those who handle me.
Out of fear of a breach in my virtue,
the sacrifice of my own life was as light to me as a blade of grass.
For me, the transgression of virtue was like leaping into the air;
[I experienced] a hundred births without interval.
I would sacrifice my life;
I would never break my virtue,
even for the sake of the four continents.
Moreover, for the sake of guarding my virtue and fulfilling the perfection of virtue,
I do not allow any alteration of mind.
"Even as he was being cast into the basket.
This concludes the second chapter, the Story of Bhūridatta.
